# Threat model: agentcore-superagent-update (Super Agent platform)

## Overview
Demo/showcase platform for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The `demo/` tree is a static React+Vite site (assessed clean). The core is `super-agent/`: a **Fastify + Prisma + PostgreSQL backend** (~50 route files, ~110 services, 67k LoC), React 19 frontend, AgentCore runtime container, AWS CDK infra, and IM gateway adapters (Slack/Telegram/Feishu/DingTalk/WeCom/WhatsApp/Discord). This assessment was isolated/local-only: all PoCs were unit- or mock-level; nothing proves production exploitability by itself.

Main components:
- `backend/src/routes/*` — ~50 REST route files; all apply `authenticate` preHandler except health/auth/IM-webhook/OAuth-callback (deliberate public surfaces)
- `backend/src/services/*` — agent runtimes (Claude SDK subprocess with `bypassPermissions`, AgentCore, OpenClaw), workflow executors, IM adapters, connectors, credential vault
- `backend/src/middleware/auth.ts` — dual-mode JWT (Cognito/local) + custom `internal.` HMAC tokens; accepts `?token=` query param
- `backend/src/websocket/execution.gateway.ts` — WebSocket gateway (confirmed: no auth on upgrade, no tenant scoping)
- `infra/` — AWS CDK; buckets/RDS properly locked down, but deploy scripts seed default admin credentials

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
- **Internet user → backend API**: bearer JWT. CONFIRMED WEAK: internal tokens are HMAC-signed with the public Cognito userPoolId in cognito mode (vuln-0001); local JWT_SECRET has a hardcoded default with no production guard (vuln-0002); default admin credentials baked into deploy scripts/docs (vuln-0005); no login rate limiting (vuln-0003). CORS reflects any origin with credentials:true (vuln-0007).
- **Authenticated member → host**: CONFIRMED WEAK: member-role users can register stdio MCP servers whose command/args/env spawn on the backend host (vuln-0015); skill names reach filesystem joins and shell command strings unvalidated (vuln-0013/0014); archive symlink members are dereferenced by fs.cp (vuln-0029).
- **Agent runtime authority**: runs `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` with a regex-denylist-only shell guard (vuln-0017); no human-confirmation gate for IM-triggered actions.
- **IM platforms → platform**: CONFIRMED WEAK: adapter signature verification fails open when no secret configured (Discord/WeCom always) (vuln-0026); binding.config plaintext secrets returned to any org member (vuln-0027).
- **Tenant ↔ tenant**: mostly enforced via BaseRepository organization_id predicates, but knowledge-base service (vuln-0016), scope memberships/plugins/connectors (vuln-0018), checkpoints/executions (vuln-0019), and the chat-room leader endpoint (vuln-0025) bypass it.
- **Public webhooks**: webhook secret generated but never verified (vuln-0011); workflow api_call nodes fetch arbitrary URLs (vuln-0009); MCP test endpoint SSRF (vuln-0010).
- **WebSocket**: `/ws/executions` has no authentication and no ownership checks (vuln-0020).

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
| Who | Start | Path | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unauthenticated | API port | default creds (vuln-0005) or forged tokens (vuln-0001/0002) → member role → stdio MCP server (vuln-0015) | host command execution |
| Unauthenticated | IM webhook URLs | fail-open signature check (vuln-0026) → message injection → agent with bypassPermissions (vuln-0017) | credentialed command execution/exfiltration |
| Unauthenticated | /ws/executions | no auth, subscribe to any executionId (vuln-0020) | cross-tenant execution data incl. node outputs |
| Unauthenticated | public webhook trigger | unverified secret (vuln-0011) → workflow with api_call node (vuln-0009) | SSRF from backend host |
| Authenticated member | zip upload / skill install | name traversal (vuln-0013) or symlink deref (vuln-0029) | arbitrary file write / out-of-bounds read |
| Authenticated member | knowledge-base / scope / checkpoint routes | missing org predicates (vuln-0016/0018/0019/0025) | cross-tenant read/modify, approval bypass |

Unrealistic: physical access; attacks on the static `demo/` site beyond client-side issues (assessed clean); anything requiring live AWS/production validation (out of scope for this isolated assessment).

## Severity Calibration
Applied: critical = unauthenticated or member-reachable full compromise (token forgery, default admin creds, MCP stdio RCE, bypassPermissions runtime). High = cross-tenant data access, arbitrary file write, unauthenticated WS data leak, symlink out-of-bounds read. Medium = SSRF, fail-open webhook verification, secret exposure, unverified-email ATO. Low/info = token-in-URL, sanitizer gaps, reliability defects (A2A hash mismatch, scheduler double-execution). Intended operations requested by authorized users are not vulnerabilities; the filed findings concern missing identity/tenant/scope enforcement on those operations.
